title: 01 — Impact wave: restore fighter occlusion
findings: The native owner computes clip coordinates, then discards clip Z in favor of NextProjectedDepth for every triangle. The original display callback selects AA_ZB_XLU_SURF. The exact asset command decode is user-supplied, not independently repeated here. Current projected source-depth and painter-transition helpers were inspected.
potential_runtime_change: Apply/review R01: cache SourceDepthToV16(z * PROJECTED_VERTEX, w) for the 18 unique vertices and emit that array per corner. Keep the current XY, UV, material, topology and source order. Independently review R02 so effect models inherit the source G_ZBUFFER state while their own clear/set masks still apply. Check the effective render-mode compare/write contract, not G_ZBUFFER alone. Full-alpha DS depth writes and near clipping are separate requirements; do not force every effect to alpha 30 as a shortcut.
falsifier: If the observed ring never engages this native owner, follow its actual owner before attributing the live symptom. A passing ring/native A/B against the old equally broken control is not an N64-reference proof.

title: 02 — Main menu: 1P mode selection
findings: The inspected board reports the 1P shipping gate remains zero while campaign implementation is active. It records a next-stage Intro allocation failure and native failures. This is not evidence that the owner still wants 1P paused.
potential_runtime_change: Keep the production gate intact until the campaign candidate is complete. On the dedicated 1P candidate, repair the natural ModeSelect -> 1P menu -> 1P CSS route and resolve the next-Intro working set: retire scene-owned CSS images/registrations before the new arena is populated, retain only explicitly persistent campaign state, and build a source-derived intro asset closure instead of an unbounded full-file duplication where feasible. Generate the campaign/native scene registration and menu capability from the same admitted build configuration. Promote the shipping gate only after complete next-stage, continue and return-path proof; do not substitute an error beep, dead row, forced arena increase or VS redirect.
falsifier: An intentionally zero shipping feature flag explains nonselectability but not invisible pixels in a separately enabled campaign build. First record both configurations and distinguish them.

title: 03 — Campaign: invisible 1P character select
findings: The named shell ROM is not sufficient to identify its compiled scene/campaign settings. The inspected board preserves active 1P work and warns about incomplete native output; no current natural 1P CSS capture was available here.
potential_runtime_change: Patch the 1P scene owner, not VS global state: acquire the native menu kit and the selected fighter preview in the 1P taskman generation; initialize its particles/effects before preview animation; run the same native body/material kernels used by a proven VS preview. Bind the 1P layout, cursor and camera explicitly. On scene reentry invalidate previous owner-image and material bindings before reuse. If the scene is reached but only a clear color appears, replace the retired text/sprite consumer with generated 1P surfaces rather than routing to a compatibility renderer. Distinguish a missing fighter-only pass from missing background/portraits before editing.
falsifier: Do not call the entire VS scene startup as a fix: that can reset campaign choice/rules and replace the 1P scene contract. A route witness without pixels leaves this report open.

title: 04 — Data menu: replace the blue-only presentation
findings: The complete DATA fragment still calls the retired text API. Original mndata.c supplies different two-row and three-row layouts, a 16*8 middle tab, source labels and a background. Options already uses the native surface API.
potential_runtime_change: R05 adds DATA surfaces at the end of the generator list, registers them in the menu coverage inventory and replaces DATA text-slot draws with native surface blits. It selects locked/unlocked row tables without changing the Sound Test unlock bit. Successful-blit caching avoids steady-state redraws and retries failed blits without publishing false visibility. Regenerate/stage mn_ui_kit and mn_surfaces together under the normal build configuration; never reuse the old manifest with the new runtime. Also audit any surface preload/classification list in the current checkout. VS Record and Sound Test child screens still need their own native surface/digit consumers; R05 does not close those children.
falsifier: If the exact local revision already has native DATA surfaces, rebase or retain that work rather than replacing it. The host mock cannot prove source sprite decoding, VRAM placement, surface bounds or menu cadence.

Complete Kirby native owner-image residency, hidden-part/root programs and copy-hat ownership before changing the CSS admission mask. Publish a fighter kind only after its FPC1 data, both reachable detail images and preview pose are valid in the same generation. Treat the copy-hat runtime tables as owned by their per-battle-slot image and retire them with their backing range. Once current full-moveset/preview evidence qualifies Kirby, update the existing canonical roster admission owner and associated generated menu cells, not save unlock bits or an independent duplicate mask.

title: 08 — VS CSS: gate-opening stalls and flashing
findings: The compact-preview action budget is already present. The acquisition still performs blocking work inside that action, so one action per tick does not bound its time. R03 closes reset-order gaps but not gate animation cost.
potential_runtime_change: Implement the bounded preview transaction in research/CSS_TRANSACTIONAL_PREVIEW.md. Split payload, relocation, native image load and pose preparation into budgeted phases; publish one complete preview identity only at a safe presentation boundary. Keep the gate animation and already-visible preview drawing while an acquisition is pending. Cache unchanged menu surfaces/matrices and avoid repeated texture uploads after residency. Attribute flashing independently: inspect BG/OBJ/GX bank ownership, generation retirement and publish order; repair the first premature visibility or stale binding rather than hiding gates or reducing simulation arbitrarily.
falsifier: If a gate-only resident run still hitches without acquisition, the bottleneck is not the loader. Profile the gate draw and display-bank commit separately. Do not add another action-budget decrement.

Keep the old disjoint shared-pin guard.

title: 10 — VS CSS: music pauses or restarts on preview changes
findings: The current acquire path explicitly brackets preview file loading with ndsAudioBgmSuspendForBlockingLoad/ResumeAfterBlockingLoad. The BGM implementation comment says resume continues rather than restarts; a heard restart still requires identifying a separate sequence-start/seek event.
potential_runtime_change: Replace the long blocking acquire with the transaction in CSS_TRANSACTIONAL_PREVIEW.md. Keep the BGM stream/file position and active mixer sequence alive while bounded file reads occur; service BGM outside the filesystem critical section with sufficient prebuffer before each slice. Cancel obsolete preview work without restarting the track. Remove the CSS suspension calls only once worst-case slice latency is below the measured buffered-audio service margin. Audit scene/BGM-start calls on hover: a hover must not imitate scene entry or invoke a stop/start sequence.
falsifier: Deleting suspension alone can turn a pause into an underrun or unsafe file reentrancy. Count pauses, actual start/seek calls and underruns separately; a monotonic stream cursor disproves a reset theory, not an audible pause.

title: 11 — VS CSS: delayed preview after cursor hover
findings: Current CSS misses perform multiple preparation steps in one acquire action. The delay may include explicit dwell, acquisition, pose warming and deferred publication; no measured breakdown from the reported ROM was available.
potential_runtime_change: Implement separate request and resident identities with cancellation/coalescing. Serve an already-resident matching preview immediately; on a miss, reserve one available resident block and stage its data in bounded chunks. Warm only source-required idle/selected poses at an admitted loading boundary, not the entire moveset on cursor movement. Publish the newest still-requested fighter only when all resources are valid; release superseded jobs without exposing partial geometry. Reduce a dwell constant only if it is the measured remaining delay after loads are bounded.
falsifier: Fast cursor input that repeatedly cancels jobs must not starve the final settled request, leak blocks or display the wrong fighter. Do not claim zero hover I/O simply from a warm-cache tour.

Bind the shell child to the source egg transform, update lifetime through the source callback, and dispatch it on its actual source link. Integrate with the same egg resource closure used by egg lay/entry only where the source actually shares assets.
falsifier: Re-enabling a formerly weak function or adding an already-present atlas sheet is not evidence. Positive source spawn plus positive native draw plus visible shell fragments are all required.

title: 16 — Link intro: translucent column effect
findings: LinkSpecial2 shows the entry wave/column as CI4 materials with distinct primitive alpha; Spin uses an IA texture. Treating every Link effect as the same IA8 decoder bug is incorrect. Existing alpha-texture conversions must be retained.

For the CI4 column, keep palette coverage separate from primitive alpha: do not turn all nonzero texels opaque or discard the animated material alpha. R02 is a separately audited candidate for source depth inheritance, not an alpha fix. Add a generated material fixture proving the source column alpha reaches the emitted polygon state; ensure state caching keys include changing alpha.
falsifier: If decoded texture alpha is correct but the quad is hard, inspect polygon/combiner state before rebaking. Conversely a wrong palette/coverage plane cannot be fixed by lowering the whole polygon alpha.

title: 19 — Pikachu neutral-B: transparent soft-edged electric effect

If effective alpha uses source vertex alpha, route it through the material owner rather than ignoring it. Keep ground-jolt root selection and material-frame changes synchronized.

Do not suppress Thunder or add a broad NULL-return bandaid as a completed fix. Use human neutral input to trigger ground/air Down-B naturally.

A bounded source-derived bias is a last candidate only when exact placement is correct and the DS mapping demonstrably loses intended coverage.

findings: The generator already subdivides source root (157,0x9D8) once before replacing per-corner alpha with a triangle average. That improves facets but cannot reproduce continuous source alpha. title: 29 — Zebes ground lights: taper to transparency
findings: The hard trapezoid can be a lost source vertex-alpha gradient, lost texture alpha or both. The existing stage generator collapses varying vertex alpha to one value per triangle; that mechanism is directly visible, but the exact light root was not independently decoded here.

For untextured SHADE-alpha lights, test E01 isobands or a source-derived alpha-ramp texture mapped to the source beam extent; for textured lights, retain the texture coverage and combine it with the varying shade factor rather than replacing one with the other. Keep the bottom bright and the top source-transparent using the original material colors and geometry. Emit native translucent polygons with the correct compare/write policy and no opaque rectangular backing.
falsifier: Do not extend the acid root allowlist to guessed light root offsets. If light alpha already resides in texels, additional geometric subdivision is not the first repair.

title: 31 — Yoshi's Island: transparent rotating texture cards

Clear atlas gutters or use correct clamping only where source sampling requires it. Keep the source rotation and visible white art.

title: 35 — Saffron City: restore the garage-door state/animation cycle
findings: The original imported state machine already owns the cycle. In Open, it calls SetClosedWait only when monster_gobj becomes NULL; SetClosedWait resets waits, position and closing animation. The gate has its own gcPlayAnimAll process. A baked open pose alone is not evidence that runtime animation is frozen.
potential_runtime_change: First compare gate_status, monster_gobj, animation frame and the submitted live gate matrix. If state remains Open after the monster should retire, repair the actual source monster-clear/ejection callback connection.
